thread:
maria: quick heads-up — security scans flagged three cluster component issues: kubelet privilege escalation vector, etcd auth bypass edge case, and cert-manager CSR validation bug. linking notes in #sec-board shortly.
ben: are these public CVEs or internal findings? how bad is the exposure?
maria: two are public (etcd & cert-manager), kubelet was flagged by our internal fuzzing with a similar exploit pattern. rough CVSS guesses: etcd ~9.1, kubelet ~8.0, cert-manager ~6.4. prioritize etcd + kubelet.
kai: +1 on prioritizing etcd. if auth bypass is real we should assume cluster compromise risk for control plane backups. any mitigations short-term?
maria: short-term mitigations I tested: disable unauthenticated access on etcd, enforce client certs on etcd listener, and lock down APIserver <-> etcd network paths. also enabled audit-policy to log etcd admin ops.
sam: can we do those without downtime? etcd config changes need rolling restart of control plane, but we can do it staged per-region. kubelet fix likely requires node kubelet binary update and node restarts.
ben: schedule wise: cert-manager patch is low-risk and should ship first (controller restart). etcd next with a small maintenance window. kubelet last since node drains are required.
maria: agreed. proposed order: 1) cert-manager patch & RBAC review, 2) etcd harden + creds rotation + backups validation, 3) kubelet binary upgrade + node rolling restart. aim to avoid mass disruption by canarying in a single region.
kai: notes on RBAC: cert-manager controller currently has broad clusterrole. we should create a scoped ClusterRole and ServiceAccount per-namespace where possible. also add audit hook for CSR approvals.
maria: noted — I opened an RBAC PR with least-privilege rules. will include migration steps: create new SA+role, deploy side-by-side, then switch.
sam: KMS note for etcd backups: rotation of envelope keys will be required if we re-encrypt snapshots. do we need to coordinate with customers using Private deployments with HSM?
ben: yes, private customers with customer-managed KMS must be notified. also snapshots stored in our backup bucket need re-encryption plan if keys rotate. add this to customer comms.
maria: I've drafted a maintenance advisory. key points: expected brief control-plane restarts for etcd, node drains for kubelet patch, cert-manager restart with no workload impact. will post to status.redwood when schedule confirmed.
deploy-bot: nightly-canary: cert-manager:v1.9.3-patch deployed to canary cluster (canary-1) at 2026-03-26T02:10Z. logs: all controllers OK.
alerts-bot: vulnerability-scanner: etdc-auth-bypass (score 9.1) detected in prod-controlplane-3 — investigation assigned to @maria.
ben: Can we get an automated test for the exploit vectors to prevent regressions?
maria: yes — adding integration tests in sec-tests repo. test will simulate malformed client cert + APIserver proxy path scenario and assert rejection.
kai: operational plan needs owners/dates. suggest: cert-manager patch (owner: maria) target: 2026-03-27T08:00Z; etcd lockdown & key rotation (owner: ben) target: 2026-03-29T22:00Z; kubelet upgrade (owner: sam) target: 2026-04-03T04:00Z.
sam: I'll coordinate node upgrade runbook: pre-checks, cordon+drain, kubelet binary swap, health probes, uncordon. will add extra slow-drain for stateful workloads.
maria: I'll follow up with PR links and status page text. also verifying whether Dedicated clusters need a different rollback plan.
ben: add a postmortem template item to capture lessons and any customer impact.
kai: sounds good. @maria please tag me on the cert-manager RBAC PR for a quick review.
maria: will do. thanks all — posting an action tracker shortly. :thumbsup:
